response.sql:
WITH global_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(f.feerate) as avg_feerate
  FROM fees f
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
),
channel_avgs AS (
  SELECT o.orderbase, AVG(f.feerate) as channel_avg
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.orderbase
)
SELECT 
  AVG(ca.channel_avg) as mean_avg_feerate,
  AVG(ca.channel_avg) - (SELECT avg_feerate FROM global_avg) as above_average
FROM channel_avgs ca
WHERE ca.channel_avg > (SELECT avg_feerate FROM global_avg);

assumptions.assumption: A channel "has an above-average fee rate" if its average fee rate (across all its fees) exceeds the global average, not merely if it contains at least one above-average fee.

alternatives.interpretation: A channel "has an above-average fee rate" if it contains at least one fee with a rate above the global average. Report the mean of all fees from such channels and how far above average they are.
alternatives.sql:
WITH global_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(f.feerate) as avg_feerate
  FROM fees f
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
),
channels_with_above_avg_fees AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.orderbase
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
  AND f.feerate > (SELECT avg_feerate FROM global_avg)
)
SELECT 
  AVG(f.feerate) as mean_avg_feerate,
  AVG(f.feerate) - (SELECT avg_feerate FROM global_avg) as above_average
FROM fees f
INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
AND o.orderbase IN (SELECT orderbase FROM channels_with_above_avg_fees);
